ruling_text:
Case Number:
25STCV14916
Hearing Date:

March 17, 2026
Dept:

MOTION FOR ORDER DEEMING SET ONE

ADMITTED
The Court tenders the following tentative decision in the
matter
Casey Kuzdrowski v. Integon Preferred Insurance Co., et al.
, Los
Angeles County Superior Court case number 25STCV14916, set for hearing on March
17, 2026. On July 31, 2025, Integon Preferred Insurance Co. (Defendant) received
requests for admissions (RFAs) propounded by Casey Kuzdrowski (Plaintiff) upon
Direct Auto Insurance. (Austin Decl. ¶ 4.) Responses were due within 30 days on
August 30. (Code Civ. Proc., § 2033.250.) Defendant indicated that the RFAs did
not name the proper party and never provided a response. (
Id.
¶¶ 5–6.) Plaintiff
filed the present motion to deem RFAs admitted on February 17, 2026. Defendant
opposes the motion. Plaintiff’s motion is denied.
“If a party to whom requests for admission are directed
fails to serve a timely response . . . [that] party waives any objection to the
requests.” (Code Civ. Proc., § 2033.280, subd. (a).) “The requesting party may
move for an order that the genuineness of any documents and the truth of any
matters specified in the requests be deemed admitted.” (
Id.
, § 2033.280,
subd. (b).) The Court shall grant an order deeming RFAs admitted unless the responding
party serves substantially compliant responses before the hearing on the
motion. A finding of substantial compliance depends on “whether answers in a
proposed response are ‘as complete and straightforward’ as reasonably possible,
as explicitly required by section 2033.220.” (
Katayama v. Continental
Investment Group
(2024) 105 Cal.App.5th 898, 907.) A party not in
possession of information or knowledge necessary to respond to a request for
admission must state in the answer that “a reasonable inquiry concerning the
matter in the particular request has been made, and that the information known
or readily obtainable is insufficient to enable that party to admit the matter.”
(Code Civ. Proc., § 2033.220, subd. (c).)
Here, the Court must determine whether RFAs were directed to
Defendant. Plaintiff’s email sent to Defendant allegedly propounding discovery
stated that the discovery requests were directed to Direct Auto Insurance.
(Austin Decl., Ex. B.) Defendant maintains that it does not do business as
Direct Auto Insurance. (
Id.
¶ 5.) Section 2033.060 mandates that the
identity of the responding party be listed in the first paragraph immediately
below the title of the case. (Code Civ. Proc., § 2033.060.) The RFAs list the
responsive party in that location as Direct Auto Insurance. (Arrasmith Decl., Ex.
A.) Because the RFAs listed the responding party as an unrelated entity,
Plaintiff has not shown that she directed the RFAs at Defendant. Thus, relief
is unavailable under section 2033.280. Accordingly, Plaintiff’s motion is
denied.

Conclusion:

The Court denies
Plaintiff’s motion.
